hook: Your ROAS target is probably wrong. Here's the 10-second maths.
outline: 1) Hook. 2) Break-even ROAS = 1 ÷ gross margin. 3) Example: £30 facial oil, £9 product+shipping+fees = 70% margin → break-even ROAS 1.43. 4) Below that you lose money on every first order. 5) Why bundles move the number (higher AOV, same ad cost). 6) CTA: comment 'ROAS' and I'll work out yours.
caption: Most skincare brands set a ROAS target by gut feel. Work out your break-even first: 1 ÷ your gross margin. Everything above it is profit; everything below it is paid-for growth. Comment ROAS and I'll calculate yours.

hook: Why I'd test a founder-story ad before another product shot
outline: 1) Product shots tell people what it is; founder stories tell them why to trust it. 2) Format: founder to camera, 1 line of origin, 1 line of what makes it different, product in hand. 3) Keep it under 20s, captions on. 4) Test it against your current best ad, same budget, same audience.
caption: If your brand has a real origin story, it's probably your most under-used ad. Here's the simple format I'd test first.

hook: 4 ASA rules every UK skincare brand should know before running ads
outline: 1) Hook. 2) Cosmetics can't claim to treat medical conditions (e.g. eczema) under the CAP Code. 3) Claims need evidence you can show. 4) The ASA has ruled against beauty filters that exaggerate results in ads. 5) 'Natural'/'clean' claims need care. 6) What you CAN say: texture, routine, ingredients, founder story. 7) CTA: save this.
caption: Getting an ad pulled costs more than writing it carefully. Four rules worth knowing before your next skincare campaign. (General guidance, not legal advice.)

hook: What I'd test on this skincare ad (respectfully)

hook: Your £25 hero product can't pay for its own ads. Here's the fix.
outline: 1) Hook. 2) Ad cost per customer is similar whether they buy £25 or £60. 3) Example maths. 4) Three bundle types: routine set, 2-pack, gift set. 5) Lead the ad with the set, not the single item. 6) CTA.
caption: Same click cost, bigger basket. Why bundles are the first lever I pull for skincare brands with low order values.

hook: 5 hooks that work for skincare brands without making claims
outline: 1) Texture close-up. 2) Ingredient count ('7 ingredients. That's it.'). 3) Founder origin line. 4) 'One product, five uses' demo. 5) Before-the-routine / after-the-routine (no filters). Each 2-3s on screen.
caption: Five hook formats you can shoot this week with your phone. No claims needed.

hook: How I'd spend your first £1,500 on Meta ads
outline: 1) Don't split it 20 ways. 2) 3 hooks × 2 offers = 6 ads. 3) One campaign, broad audience, let the algorithm find buyers. 4) Kill/keep rules after enough spend. 5) What you learn even if nothing wins.
caption: A simple testing plan for a small budget, so every pound teaches you something.

hook: 5 paid-ads mistakes I see on indie skincare stores
outline: 1) Hook. 2) Sending ads to the homepage. 3) No bundle or set to raise order value. 4) One ad running for months (creative fatigue). 5) Tracking not checked (pixel/Conversions API). CTA.
caption: None of these need a bigger budget to fix.
